name: liminality

attributes.attribute: a day of widened access to the Otherworld

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Celts saw the world as lying beside an Otherworld. That other land held the dead, the gods, and the fairy folk. Certain times and places opened a way between the two. Twilight, dawn, and the turn of the year were doors. Lakes, mists, and bogs marked a low border. These in-between spots drew danger and wonder. The year's great days of Samhain and Beltane stood open to the Otherworld. A lone traveler near a fairy mound on those days could be taken.

okr.objective: Describe the Celtic border places that open into the Otherworld.
key_results: The Celts held that a parallel Otherworld touched their own.
Certain days and places stood open between the worlds.
Bogs, lakes, and mist sat low as boundaries.
Samhain special times put a person at greater risk near a mound.
